newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka renews call for peace talks with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka renews call for peace talks with rebels.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has reitrated that she is ready to resume peace talks with Tamil Tiger rebels, possibly with third party mediation, the Sunday Observer newspaper said.

But Kumaratunga told the newspaper in an interview that talks can be resumed only if the rebels indicate their willingness to lay down arms and agree to a fixed and limited time frame for the dialogue.
"We gave them almost everything they wanted, but they kicked us in the teeth," she said in the interview.

Kumaratunga said that she was insisting on the two conditions because the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had reneged on previous ceasefires and used the time to regroup and prepare for further hostilities.
"Now it is clear that unless (LTTE chief Velupillai) Prabhakaran is so weakened that he has no other option, they are not likely to seriously enter into a dialogue," she said.
The government has mounted several major offensives against the rebels, capturing their northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold and confining the Tigers largely to their jungle bases.

Defence spending this year has soared to almost 50 billion rupees ($877 million) compared to 32 billion rupees ($561 million) in 1995, when the Tigers torpedoed peace talks by sinking two navy gunboats in a suicide attack in the eastern port of Trincomalee.

The government has said it wants to weaken the rebels militarily and force them back to the negotiating table in an effort to end the war, now in its 14th year, in which more than 50,000 people have died.

Kumaratunga said the government had received many offers from foreign governments, institutions and individuals to help mediate an end to the war by the LTTE for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
